thread:
support-l1: Customer ACME (ticket ACME-241) reports streaming responses cut off mid-stream. Client shows "broken pipe" and accounting counted a 5xx. req=req_abcd1234, route=/v1/streams/generate, model=redwood-13b-v1. They provided a curl repro and tcpdump.

Sam K: can you paste the exact curl + request id + any gateway logs? want to see whether this is client abort vs server error.

support-l1: curl they used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"prompt":"hello", "stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
# they hit ctrl-c after ~4s and get broken pipe locally
```
request_id=req_abcd1234, tcpdump attached (pcap).

Ingrid M: pasted gateway log snippets for req_abcd1234 (redacted):
```
[2024-09-14T12:11:09Z] req=req_abcd1234 upstream_write: wrote 1024 bytes
[2024-09-14T12:11:10Z] req=req_abcd1234 upstream_write: wrote 1024 bytes
[2024-09-14T12:11:11Z] req=req_abcd1234 upstream_write: write failed: EPIPE
[2024-09-14T12:11:11Z] req=req_abcd1234 proxy: upstream connection closed during streaming, classifying 502
```

Ingrid M: tcpdump shows client FIN rather than RST. semantics: kernel returns EPIPE on write after peer FIN. current proxy treats any write failure as upstream error -> 5xx.

Sam K: quick hypothesis: client abort via FIN then we hit EPIPE on write and our gateway marks 502. If bytes were already sent to client (they received partial SSE frames), we should treat as CLIENT_DISCONNECT not server failure. This matters for billing and ops metrics.

ops-l2: I reproduced with a tiny python socket client that closes mid-stream (FIN). snippet:
```
import socket, ssl, time
s = socket.create_connection(('api.redwood.ai', 443))
# TLS handshake layer omitted in snippet
s.send(b'GET /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.ai\r\nAccept: text/event-stream\r\n\r\n')
# read a couple of SSE events
time.sleep(2)
s.close()  # triggers FIN from client side
```
Result: upstream write path sees EPIPE and proxy returns 502 in logs.

Elaine C: customer is asking for credits because they received partial output but our billing shows 5xx. Can CS offer a temporary goodwill credit while engineering investigates?

Ingrid M: engineering decision options:
1) Leave as-is: EPIPE -> 5xx. Simple but billing disputes keep coming.
2) Heuristic: if write fails with EPIPE AND bytes_sent > 0 (or stream_started flag true), classify as CLIENT_ABORT and do not count as 5xx.
3) Require tcp-level checks (FIN vs RST) to decide. More correct but slower and platform dependent.

Sam K: preference for option 2 short-term: it's straightforward and handles the common case where clients ctrl-c. We'll add telemetry label client_disconnect_fin when we detect FIN before write error. Also a regression test.

ops-l2: for short-term metrics we can exclude these hits from 5xx dashboards and from billing-extract. I can push a Prom rule to mark these and a temporary billing EXCLUDE for the affected window.

Ingrid M: I'll draft a small gateway patch: on write error EPIPE/EHOSTUNREACH path check stream_started flag or bytes_sent. If true -> mark X-Stream-Disconnect: client and set response_code classification to CLIENT_ABORT (no server_5xx increment). Emit metric server.request_disconnect_type=client_fin. Unit tests + code owner review required.

support-l1: CS staged a customer message offering an interim credit and asked for a postmortem once fixed.

deploy-bot: planned rollout gateway/1.43.0 -> 1.43.1 (classification fix). Canary in us-west-2 scheduled 2024-09-15T03:00Z.

ops-l2: canary deployed to us-west-2 canary group. Observed: streaming route 5xx rate dropped 0.08% in that pool within 10m. Logs now include label server.request_disconnect_type=client_fin for matching requests. No increase in "real" upstream errors.

Sam K: merged PR, added unit tests for EPIPE & FIN detection, and an integration test where client closes after N SSE events asserting no server_5xx counter increment.

Ingrid M: rolled out globally 2024-09-15T04:20Z. Backfilled metrics for the last 48h to avoid a billing spike. Added diagnostic header X-Client-Disconnect: fin to aid support.

Elaine C: finance issued a pro-rated credit for ACME for the affected calls; FIN-3982. Customer confirmed partial payload was useful and accepted credit.

support-l1: closing ACME-241, added postmortem link https://redwood.internal/CS/ACME-241-postmortem and flagged for quarterly audit.

ops-l2: follow-up action: add monthly alert that samples streaming 5xx spikes and auto-saves tcpdumps for top-5 customers to detect similar patterns proactively.

Sam K: thanks all. leaving thread. :+1:
